title: Derived sections on the basis detect isomorphisms
statement: Let $X$ be an affine scheme and $R$ a commutative ring. Use the small skeleton and universes of the small pro-etale site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and the constant sheaf of rings $R_X$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R_X)$, the category of sheaves of $R_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and let $D^+(\mathcal A)$ be its bounded-below derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. Let $\mathcal B_X$ be the affine ind-etale subsite of [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis]. For $W\in\mathcal B_X$, write $R\Gamma(W,-)$ for the right derived evaluation functor: represent an object by a bounded-below complex $I^\bullet$ of injective objects of $\mathcal A$ and take $\Gamma(W,I^\bullet)$ in $D^+(R_X(W)\text{-}\operatorname{Mod})$. Equivalently it is derived global sections after restriction to $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives]. If $u:K\to L$ is a morphism in $D^+(\mathcal A)$ and $R\Gamma(W,u)$ is an isomorphism for every $W\in\mathcal B_X$, then $u$ is an isomorphism in $D^+(\mathcal A)$.

proof.text: Use the Grothendieck abelian structure on module sheaves [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] and enough injectives [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] to both bounded-below objects. By K-injectivity and [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], represent the conjugate of the given morphism by a homotopy class and lift that class to a chain map a between the injective representatives.

For each affine basis object, use the units of Mathlib rightDerivedFunctorPlus. These units are invertible on bounded-below complexes of injectives, so their naturality identifies the localized evaluation of a with the derived evaluation of its localized image. The hypothesis makes the latter invertible. The localization of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] reflects quasi-isomorphisms, so every evaluated a is a quasi-isomorphism. This uses the definition of derived evaluation itself and does not pass through restriction to a slice site.

Let T be the forgetful functor from module sheaves to abelian sheaves of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], U the inclusion into abelian presheaves, and S abelian sheafification. The functor T is exact and reflects isomorphisms. Exactness of S [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact] gives a natural isomorphism between sheafified presheaf homology of (T followed by U) applied to a complex and homology of its S-image. The sheafification counit identifies (T followed by U) followed by S with T. Exactness of T then identifies this homology with T applied to module-sheaf homology. This is the kernel-image calculation of Stacks Tag 0BKV and is formalized as sheafifiedHomologyIso; no exactness of U or sheaf evaluation is required.

For every degree n let g be the presheaf homology map of the underlying presheaf-complex map. Presheaf evaluation and forgetting from modules to abelian groups are exact. Step 2 therefore implies that g restricted to the affine basis is objectwise invertible. The dense-subsite comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-basis], expressed by GrothendieckTopology.W_whiskerLeft_iff, makes g invertible after sheafification. Apply the same comparison to the AsSmall equivalence to transport between the original pro-etale site and the chosen small model. Step 3 makes the module-sheaf homology maps invertible, since T reflects isomorphisms. Thus a is a quasi-isomorphism. This is formalized as quasiIso_of_basis_evaluation.

By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] the localization sends a to an isomorphism. The inclusion of the bounded-below derived category into the derived category reflects isomorphisms. Conjugate back by the two chosen isomorphisms of step 1 to conclude that the original morphism is invertible.

proof_origin.place: Proof, direct homology-map version of the kernel-image/sheafification argument of Stacks Tag 0BKV; Mathlib injective representatives, right-derived-functor units and dense-subsite comparison. Formalized by T3 on 2026-10-19.
